primitives.name: Methodological Framework for Sports ML
primitives.verbatim_quote: After outlining repeatable search terms and inclusion criteria, we offer a thematic synthesis arranged by task family (recognition/segmentation, tracking and pose, tactical decision support, biomechanics/engineering prediction, and health/injury risk) and data modality (wearables, clinical/screening data, video, and tracking).
primitives.assumptions: Task families and data modalities are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive for describing sports ML applications.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When task families overlap or data modalities are insufficiently represented.

layer2.mapping: The thematic synthesis maps directly to GSI's structured knowledge base where task families correspond to inference modules and data modalities define input channels.
layer2.telemetry: Study inclusion rate per task family and data modality.

primitives.name: Predictive Modeling in Sports Medicine
primitives.verbatim_quote: This includes predictive modelling for sports medicine and athlete monitoring using wearables and screening data, sequential modelling for trajectory prediction, and computer vision for broadcast understanding (event spotting, multi-object tracking, pose estimation).
primitives.assumptions: Predictive models assume stationary environments and sufficient historical data for training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In cases of non-stationary athlete states or sparse data availability.

layer2.mapping: Derived from wearable sensor data and clinical inputs, this kernel enables GSI's health risk scoring engine.
layer2.telemetry: Injury prediction accuracy and false positive rates.

primitives.name: Video Understanding Benchmarks
primitives.verbatim_quote: For example, the release of SoccerNet-v2 improved our understanding of broadcast soccer by adding ~300k annotations to 500 untrimmed matches and testing several tasks (action spotting, camera shot segmentation, and replay grounding).
primitives.assumptions: Benchmark datasets provide standardized evaluation metrics for video understanding tasks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When benchmark datasets lack diversity or fail to represent real-world variability.

layer2.mapping: SoccerNet-v2 annotations align with GSE's video event detection and replay grounding modules.
layer2.telemetry: Annotation coverage and task-specific F1 scores.

primitives.assumptions: Roles and ball interaction are deterministic within tactical frameworks.

primitives.name: Supervised Prediction Using Trajectory and RGB Cues
primitives.verbatim_quote: framed a supervised prediction problem using both trajectory and RGB cues: the dataset comprised 15,586 scenes (train/val/test splits reported), and the proposed combined trajectory + RGB approach achieved top-1 accuracy 62.5% (top-3 92.3%, top-5 97.5%)—a large jump over nearest-player and CNN baselines (Honda, 2022).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'Prediction task', 'T': 'Trajectory cue', 'R': 'RGB cue', 'A': 'Accuracy metric', 'S': 'Scene dataset size'}
primitives.assumptions: Trajectory and RGB cues are jointly informative; model is trained end-to-end.

layer2.mapping: Joint likelihood function in GSI's predictive model combining visual and motion features.
layer2.telemetry: Top-k accuracy scores on test set.

primitives.name: Inverse Reward Inference Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: / Machine learning trends in sport: Systematic review Journal of Human Sport & Exercise VOLUME 21 | ISSUE 3 | 2026 | 987 IRL methods address sparse rewards by inferring dense reward surrogates from demonstrations.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R(s,a): Dense surrogate reward function (dimensionless utility). D: Demonstration trajectory set. P(a|s): Policy distribution.
primitives.assumptions: Demonstrations are generated by a rational agent maximizing an unknown reward function; the state-action space is sufficiently covered by the demonstration set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when demonstrations exhibit sub-optimal play or when the true reward function relies on unobserved latent variables outside the feature space.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's tactical valuation layer, converting sparse win/loss outcomes into granular, state-specific utility gradients.

primitives.name: High-Frequency Sensing Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Wearables, IoT, and physiological/biomechanical modelling Wearables-driven sports ML often confronts smaller n but higher-frequency sensing, requiring careful feature representation and latency-aware design.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: n: Sample size (dimensionless count). f_s: Sampling frequency (Hz). t_latency: Inference delay (seconds).
primitives.assumptions: Signal-to-noise ratio remains stable at high frequencies; sensor drift is negligible over the observation window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under severe motion artifacts exceeding sensor dynamic range or when computational latency exceeds the temporal resolution of the athletic movement.

layer2.mapping: Forms the foundational data ingestion layer for GSI's physiological tracking, requiring dimensionality reduction before Bayesian updating.
layer2.telemetry: Feature extraction fidelity and end-to-end pipeline latency measured in milliseconds.

primitives.name: Bayesian Biomechanical Regression
primitives.verbatim_quote: modelled ball velocity with hierarchical/Bayesian regression using IMUs on pelvis and sternum and radar-gun labels; 25 youth pitchers performed 10 maximal pitches each, and the full model achieved R2 0.975 with RMSE 0.014 (as reported in their comparison table) (Gomaz, 2021).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: v_ball: Ball velocity (m/s). a_pelvis: Pelvic acceleration (m/s^2). omega_sternum: Sternum angular velocity (rad/s). beta: Regression coefficients (dimensionally consistent).
primitives.assumptions: Kinematic chain energy transfer is linearizable locally; radar measurements provide unbiased ground truth labels.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if IMU placement shifts significantly, altering the geometric relationship between body segment kinematics and release velocity.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's hierarchical player capability modeling, where individual biomechanical priors are pooled to estimate population-level performance distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Coefficient of determination (R^2) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) against radar telemetry.

primitives.name: Stratified Clinical Recovery Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: In adolescent sports-related concussion recovery prediction, sex-stratified ML models were trained using multi-part clinical measures (including VOMS, King-Devick, and C3 Logix Trails); gradient-boosted decision-tree algorithms achieved AUC 0.84 (males) and 0.78 (females) for predicting protracted recovery, improving over statistical baselines (Chu, 2022).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Y: Protracted recovery binary outcome (dimensionless). X: Vector of clinical measures. S: Sex stratification variable (categorical). h_t: Weak learner decision stump.
primitives.assumptions: Sex is a primary causal moderator of recovery trajectories; clinical measures are collected without systematic bias across strata.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model generalization collapses if applied to demographics outside the adolescent cohort or if clinical assessment protocols change significantly.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's injury risk stratification module, enforcing conditional independence assumptions within specific demographic sub-populations to reduce confounding variance.
layer2.telemetry: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) stratified by demographic groups.

layer2.mapping: The conceptual framework aligns data modalities (video, wearable, tracking) with task families (spotting, segmentation, forecasting) via ML paradigms (CNNs, ensembles, RL).
layer2.telemetry: Benchmark accuracy on SoccerNet-v2 and FineGym datasets.

primitives.name: Deep Learning Vision Pipelines for Sports Understanding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Video data primarily supports event spotting, segmentation, tracking, and pose estimation using deep convolutional and transformer-based architectures.
primitives.assumptions: Vision-based tasks require high-resolution temporal data and spatial attention mechanisms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance drops under occlusion or fast motion due to limited temporal resolution.

layer2.mapping: Vision kernels derived from CNNs and transformers encode spatiotemporal features for event spotting and pose estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of pose estimation on SoccerNet-Tracking dataset.

primitives.name: Ensemble Methods for Wearable and Bio Signal Data
primitives.verbatim_quote: Wearable and bio signal data are commonly analysed using classical and ensemble methods for classification and regression tasks.
primitives.assumptions: Bio-signals are modeled as stochastic processes with low signal-to-noise ratios.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ensemble methods fail when data is highly skewed or lacks sufficient labeled examples.

layer2.mapping: Ensemble kernels aggregate weak learners to improve classification/regression robustness for bio-data.
layer2.telemetry: Injury prediction accuracy using boosting models on NHL player data.

primitives.name: Hybrid Modeling with Physical Constraints
primitives.verbatim_quote: The rise of hybrid modelling is a second trend: learning with constraints or priors is often beneficial for sports problems.
primitives.assumptions: Physical laws and domain knowledge enhance generalization in constrained environments.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Hybrid models fail when physical priors are misapplied or inconsistent with observed behavior.

layer2.mapping: Physics-informed kernels integrate kinematic and geometric constraints into deep learning pipelines.
layer2.telemetry: Trajectory reconstruction accuracy in badminton using MonoTrack pipeline.
